data.name: Heading
data.comment: The section's heading.

data.name: ModesName
data.comment: Name of the segmented control that picks the mode.

data.name: ModePerSecond
data.comment: The first mode: frames per second.

data.name: ModeLength
data.comment: The second mode: a target length.

data.name: ModePerPhoto
data.comment: The third mode: seconds for each photo.

data.name: PresetsFramesPerSecond
data.comment: Name of the presets in Per second mode.

data.name: PresetsLength
data.comment: Name of the presets in Length mode.

data.name: PresetsSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: Name of the presets in Per photo mode.

data.name: CustomFramesPerSecond
data.comment: The caption above the box in Per second mode (it is also the box's name for a screen reader).

data.name: CustomLength
data.comment: The caption above the box in Length mode.

data.name: CustomSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: The caption above the box in Per photo mode.

data.name: UnitFramesPerSecond
data.comment: The unit after the box in Per second mode.

data.name: UnitLength
data.comment: The unit after the box in Length mode.

data.name: UnitSecondsPerPhoto
data.comment: The unit after the box in Per photo mode.

data.name: LengthPreset
data.comment: A preset of the Length mode. {0}: the seconds ("30").

data.name: BarStart
data.comment: The bar's left end: no time.

data.name: BarMiddle
data.comment: The bar's middle: half a minute.

data.name: BarEnd
data.comment: The bar's right end: a minute, the longest clip it can show.

data.name: NotANumberFramesPerSecond
data.value: Type a frame rate from {0} to {1} fps, like 24 or {2}.
data.comment: The Per second box was left with something that is not a number. {0}: the lowest rate, {1}: the highest, {2}: the NTSC example ("29.97").

data.name: NotANumberLength
data.value: Type a length in seconds, like 30, or as minutes and seconds, like 1:30. It can be from {0} to {1}.
data.comment: The Length box was left with something that is not a length. {0}: the shortest length ("0.1 s"), {1}: the longest.

data.name: NotANumberSecondsPerPhoto
data.value: Type how many seconds each photo stays, from {0} to {1}.
data.comment: The Per photo box was left with something that is not a number. {0}: the shortest time, {1}: the longest.

data.name: ClampedFramesPerSecond
data.value: Frame rates run from {2} to {3} fps, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: A frame rate outside the range was typed. {0}: what was typed, {1}: the value now set ("120 fps"), {2}: the lowest, {3}: the highest.

data.name: ClampedLength
data.value: A video can be from {2} to {3} long, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: A length outside the range was typed. {0}: what was typed, {1}: the value now set ("0.1 s"), {2}: the shortest, {3}: the longest.

data.name: ClampedSecondsPerPhoto
data.value: A photo can stay from {2} to {3}, so {0} is now {1}.
data.comment: A time per photo outside the range was typed. {0}: what was typed, {1}: the value now set, {2}: the shortest, {3}: the longest.

data.name: NtscRate
data.comment: A frame rate typed in digits became the exact NTSC rate. {0}: the rate ("29.97 fps"), {1}: its numerator, {2}: its denominator.

data.name: ThousandsSeparator
data.value: Type 1000 without a separator, or {0} for one and a half.
data.comment: One separator followed by exactly three digits was typed ("1,000"); it is refused rather than guessed. {0}: one and a half in the user's culture ("1.5").

data.name: Rounded
data.comment: More decimals were typed than the box keeps. {0}: the value kept ("37.48 fps").

data.name: LengthTooShort
data.value: Your photos can't play in {0}: the fastest speed is {1}, so the video is {2} long.
data.comment: Length mode, the photos cannot play in the target even at the fastest speed. {0}: the target ("30 s"), {1}: the fastest speed ("120 fps"), {2}: the length the video has instead.

data.name: LengthTooLong
data.value: Your photos can't fill {0}: the slowest speed is {1}, so the video is {2} long.
data.comment: Length mode, the photos cannot fill the target even at the slowest speed. {0}: the target, {1}: the slowest speed ("10 s per photo"), {2}: the length the video has instead.
